script: I booked him a room, but his bank app shows a betrayal.. The first thing that happened was me swiping the screen to confirm the reservation for July 24‑25, then the guy flicking his phone over to show me a cheaper deal he'd found online. He swiped back to my screen, looking like he'd just discovered a secret level in a game. I said, "Bruh, that's for tomorrow, not tonight. This room's full, that's why it's $58." He didn't blink. He made the reservation anyway because he needed a spot for tomorrow too. I got the email, the payment cleared, and it was all good—except the $58 room for tonight was still unpaid. He didn't get it. He kept staring at his phone, scrolling through emails and his bank app, like he was trying to find a loophole. I tried to explain, but Spanish was a barrier and Google Translate was glitchy. He kept pulling up a screenshot that read "$40 paid," which was actually for tomorrow's room. "Can I sleep tonight?" he asked, eyes on his phone. "Yes, if you pay the room for tonight," I replied. "But I paid," he insisted, showing me the screenshot again. "Yes, that's the room for tomorrow." I said. He stared at his phone, silent, then repeated the question. The whole conversation was a loop of "I paid" vs. "I am paying." I finally told him the truth: the 12‑person dorm was full, there were no beds left. He'd tried to use his buddy's room, but that was a no‑go. He sat there, scrolling, waiting. I had a five‑minute timeout. He sighed, went back to the desk, handed over his card. I gave him the keycard, the rule sheet, and the room number. He left for his room, and the whole hour of arguing ended in less than a minute of payment. The lesson? I am the one who knows the price, the rules, and the truth. He just wanted a place to sleep, but he didn't get the "pay first" part. I am better at this than he is. (I know, right?)
